blocks.tamil_translation: narrates: “A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked, “O Rasulullah, how many times should I forgive the fault of (my) servant?” The Prophet ﷺ remained silent. He again asked in the same way, “O Rasulullah, how many times should I forgive the fault of (my) servant?” and Rasulullah ﷺ said, “Seventy times every day.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ حُذَيْفَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ يَقُوْلُ: اِنَّ رَجُلاً كَانَ فِيْمَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ اَتَاهُ الْمَلَكُ لِيَقْبِضَ رُوْحَهُ فَقِيْلَ لَهُ: هَلْ عَمِلْتَ مِنْ خَيْرٍ؟ قَالَ: مَااَعْلَمُ، قِيْلَ لَهُ: اُنْظُرْ، قَالَ: مَااَعْلَمُ شَيْئًا غَيْرَ اَنِّيْ كُنْتُ اُبَايِعُ النَّاسَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَاُجَازِيْهِمْ فَاُنْظِرُ الْمُوْسِرَ وَاَتَجَاوَزُ عَنِ الْمُعْسِرِ،فَاَدْخَلَهُ اللهُ الْجَنَّةَ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه البخاري باب ماذكر عن بني اسرائيل رقم:٣٤٥١
blocks.tamil_translation: “There was a man in a nation that went before you. The angel came to take his soul. Then he was asked, “Did you do any good deed in the world?” He said, “As far as I know, there is no (such) deed.” He was told, “Think about your lifetime.” He again said, “As far as I know, there is no (such) deed; however, there is one deed. When I did business with people in the world, giving and taking, I would give time to the wealthy and forgive the poor and needy.” Because of that, Allah Ta'ala admitted him into Jannah” — Hazrat Hudhaifah (RA) narrates that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say this.

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ قَتَادَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُوْلَ اللهِ ﷺ يَقُوْلُ: مَنْ سَرَّهُ اَنْ يُنْجِيَهُ اللهُ مِنْ كُرَبِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَلْيُنَفِّسْ عَنْ مُعْسِرٍ اَوْ يَضَعْ
